{
  "overview": "This chapter defines foundation LLMs as general-purpose models with limitations for specific tasks, explaining how fine-tuning adapts them to applications while distillation optimizes them into smaller, faster versions. It contrasts standard parameter updates with efficient tuning methods and addresses the resource costs of large models versus the accuracy trade-offs in distilled ones. The text details bulk inference distillation where teacher models generate rich numerical labels for student models, alongside prompt engineering techniques (zero-shot, one-shot, few-shot) that customize outputs without altering parameters. Finally, it compares online and offline inference strategies, citing Google Search's cached predictions for low-frequency tasks while emphasizing ethical considerations regarding model biases.",
  "topics": [
    "Foundation LLM definition and general capabilities",
    "Limitations of foundation models for specific ML tasks",
    "Fine-tuning mechanisms: standard vs. parameter-efficient approaches",
    "Training data requirements and computational costs",
    "Distillation process: creating smaller, faster models",
    "Trade-off between model size/parameters and prediction accuracy",
    "Bulk inference distillation: teacher-student dynamics",
    "Richness of numerical vs. binary labeling signals",
    "Prompt engineering: zero-shot, one-shot, and few-shot techniques",
    "Online vs. offline inference methods",
    "Resource efficiency in static/bulk inference deployments",
    "Ethical usage and inherent model biases"
  ]
}
